title: Migrate service recovery to generic AgentCore runtime
purpose: Prove the runtime foundation by replacing the hand-coded service recovery orchestration path with a generic AgentCore PlanRun.
scope: Represent nginx service recovery as a PlanSpec produced by Planner.
Run diagnostics, restart approval, restart execution, verification, and summary through AgentCore.
Keep existing semantic tools, policy decisions, leases, sandbox profiles, audit events, and verification behavior.
Deprecate or wrap the old ServiceRecoveryWorkflow so it uses AgentCore instead of owning orchestration.
Keep denied restart path and read-only diagnostics behavior unchanged.
deliverables: Compatibility tests for existing service recovery behavior
acceptance_criteria: Existing service recovery happy-path tests pass through AgentCore.
Denied restart path prepares no restart effect.
Audit timeline includes IntentReceived, PlanFrozen, policy decisions, approval, lease, EffectPrepared, EffectObserved, CommitSealed, and final summary.
The final operator explanation is grounded in observations, not model claims.
No workflow-specific code bypasses AgentCore for tool execution.
verification: Run CLI service recovery demo in approved and denied modes.
Inspect audit.show last-run for generic runtime events.
risk_notes: This is the main proof that AgentOS has a reusable bottom agent rather than a set of scripts.
